flagged.evidence: The page calls α=β=(2) the “smallest non-trivial Kronecker product” with visible small-rank stability. The current compatibility lemma and all-rank expansion give, for the smaller nonempty pair α=β=(1), R=1+s_(1)+s_(2)+s_(1,1), and products s_(1,1)*s_(1,1)=s_(2), s_(2,1)*s_(2,1)=s_(3)+s_(2,1)+s_(1,1,1), and s_(3,1)*s_(3,1)=s_(4)+s_(3,1)+s_(2,2)+s_(2,1,1). The current threshold theorem gives exact global threshold 4 for this pair, so the stated minimality is false absent an unstated restriction.

The proof says “The first letter of its reading word is the rightmost cell of the first skew row” without excluding β=∅. Then (α+β)/α is empty and its LR tableau has an empty reading word, so there is no first letter to force the row entries to be 1. The empty-input case is handled later in Proof 4.1, making this a nonfatal gap in this argument.
